subject: Transportation Systems
title: Noise and Public Acceptance
description: A micro-lesson that makes Noise and Public Acceptance usable.

hook.text: Helicopters are loud enough to annoy entire neighborhoods. eVTOLs must be dramatically quieter to succeed.

buildup.text: Multiple small rotors spread the noise across frequencies, making eVTOLs quieter than helicopters.

discovery.text: At cruise altitude, leading eVTOL designs are roughly as loud as a dishwasher. Takeoff is still noticeable.

twist.text: Even moderate noise from dozens of daily flights could turn neighborhoods against vertiport proposals.

climax.text: Companies are investing heavily in blade design and sound insulation. Quiet enough is a survival requirement.

punchline.text: The quieter the aircraft, the more landing sites it can use.

quiz.question: Why must eVTOLs be much quieter than helicopters?
options: Community noise opposition could block vertiport locations
